stories.title: The Tortoise and the Hare
stories.author: Aesop
stories.blurb: Slow and steady can win the race.
stories.imageAlt: A tortoise and a hare racing, illustration by Milo Winter

advanced.title: The Tortoise and the Hare
advanced.moral: Slow and steady wins the race.

pages.imageAlt: A proud hare and a slow tortoise meet on a sunny path
advanced: A Hare liked to tease a Tortoise for being so slow.
“I am the fastest!” said the Hare. “You could never beat me.”

pages.imageAlt: The tortoise challenges the hare to a race
advanced: The Hare laughed, but he said yes. They lined up, and the race began.

pages.imageAlt: The hare naps while the tortoise keeps walking
beginner: Then the hare takes a nap.
advanced: The Hare ran far ahead. Then he lay down for a nap. “The Tortoise is so slow,” he thought. “I have plenty of time.”
The Tortoise kept walking, step by step. He did not stop.

pages.imageAlt: The tortoise crosses the finish line first
advanced: When the Hare woke up, he ran as fast as he could. But the Tortoise had already crossed the finish line.

stories.title: The Lion and the Mouse
stories.author: Aesop
stories.blurb: A tiny friend can help a big one.
stories.imageAlt: A lion and a mouse, illustration by Milo Winter

advanced.title: The Lion and the Mouse
advanced.moral: Little friends may prove great friends.

pages.imageAlt: A big lion naps while a little mouse runs nearby
beginner: A big lion naps in the sun.
advanced: One day a Lion was sleeping in the sun. A little Mouse ran across his nose.

pages.imageAlt: The lion catches the mouse, who asks to be set free
beginner: The lion wakes up. He grabs the mouse.
“Let me go!” says the mouse. “I can help you.”
advanced: The Lion woke up and caught the Mouse with his big paw.
“Please let me go!” cried the Mouse. “Someday I may help you.”

pages.imageAlt: The lion frees the mouse, then later is trapped in a net
beginner: The lion lets the mouse go.
Later, men trap the lion in a net.
advanced: The Lion laughed. How could a tiny Mouse help a Lion? But he let the Mouse go.
Later, hunters caught the Lion in a strong net. He could not get free.

pages.imageAlt: The mouse chews the ropes and frees the lion
advanced: The little Mouse heard the Lion roar. She ran to help.
She chewed and chewed on the ropes until the Lion was free.
“Thank you, little friend,” said the Lion. “You were right!”

stories.title: The Fox and the Grapes
stories.author: Aesop
stories.blurb: What we cannot reach may seem sour.
stories.imageAlt: A fox looking up at grapes, illustration by Milo Winter

beginner.title: The Fox and the Grapes
beginner.moral: Do not hate what you cannot get.

advanced.title: The Fox and the Grapes
advanced.moral: It is easy to hate what you cannot get.

pages.imageAlt: A hungry fox looks up at grapes on a vine
advanced: A hungry Fox saw some sweet grapes hanging high on a vine.

pages.imageAlt: The fox jumps trying to reach the grapes
advanced: “Those grapes look perfect,” said the Fox. “I will get some.”
He jumped and jumped, but the grapes were too high.

pages.imageAlt: The fox fails to reach the grapes again and again
advanced: He tried again and again. Still he could not reach them.

pages.imageAlt: The fox walks away saying the grapes are sour
beginner: But he just cannot reach them.
advanced: At last the Fox walked away. “Those grapes are probably sour,” he said.
But really, he only said that because he could not have them.

stories.title: The Ant and the Grasshopper
stories.author: Aesop
stories.blurb: Work today to be ready for tomorrow.
stories.imageAlt: An ant and a grasshopper, illustration by Milo Winter

advanced.title: The Ant and the Grasshopper
advanced.moral: It is best to prepare for the days of need.

pages.imageAlt: A busy ant carries food to her nest
beginner: She puts food in her nest.
advanced: All summer, an Ant worked hard. She carried food to her nest.

pages.imageAlt: A grasshopper sings and asks the ant to play
beginner: A grasshopper sings in the sun.
advanced: A Grasshopper sang and played in the warm sun.
“Why work so hard?” asked the Grasshopper. “Come and sing with me!”

pages.imageAlt: The ant keeps working while winter approaches
advanced: “I am storing food for winter,” said the Ant. “You should do the same.”
But the Grasshopper only laughed and kept on singing.

pages.imageAlt: In winter the grasshopper is hungry and the ant has food
advanced: When winter came, the ground was cold and bare. The Grasshopper had nothing to eat.
He went to the Ant. “Please share your food,” he said.
The Ant had worked all summer, so she had food. The Grasshopper wished he had worked too.

stories.title: The Boy Who Cried Wolf
stories.author: Aesop
stories.blurb: People stop listening when we tell fibs.
stories.imageAlt: A shepherd boy calling for help, illustration by Milo Winter

advanced.title: The Boy Who Cried Wolf
advanced.moral: Liars are not believed even when they speak the truth.

pages.imageAlt: A shepherd boy watches sheep near a forest
advanced: A Shepherd Boy watched sheep near a dark forest. He felt bored.

pages.imageAlt: The boy falsely cries wolf and villagers come running
advanced: To amuse himself, he ran toward the village and shouted, “Wolf! Wolf!”
The villagers came running to help. But there was no wolf. The boy laughed.

pages.imageAlt: The boy tricks the villagers again
beginner: There is no wolf. The boy laughs.
He yells again. Men run. No wolf.
advanced: A few days later, he did it again. “Wolf! Wolf!” The villagers ran to help, and again he laughed.

pages.imageAlt: A real wolf appears and nobody comes to help
advanced: Then one evening, a real wolf came out of the forest!
The boy shouted, “Wolf! Wolf!” But this time the villagers did not come.
“He cannot fool us again,” they said.
The wolf scared the sheep, and the boy learned a hard lesson: if you tell fibs, people may not believe you when you tell the truth.
